packs.name: agent-toolkit
packs.description: A Claude Code marketplace manifest through which one steward's skills, agents, and slash commands are each installed separately.
packs.installs: A Claude Code marketplace manifest at .claude-plugin/marketplace.json, registered with /plugin marketplace add and then installed entry by entry with /plugin install <name>@agent-toolkit; each entry names a source directory under dist/plugins/, which scripts/build_plugins.py generates from the repository's skills/, agents/, and commands/ trees. The README also documents npx skills add softaworks/agent-toolkit for Agent Skills hosts and cp -r skills/<name> ~/.claude/skills/ by hand. This record pins the manifest and does not list, count, or review its entries.
packs.distribution_machinery: scripts/build_plugins.py generates the dist/plugins/ tree the manifest resolves against, and scripts/bump_version.py raises the manifest version. Neither is installed into a host; both operate on the repository's own files.
packs.not_a_system: A marketplace manifest that lists other packs for installation; it is an install source, not a system, and this record never lists, counts, or reviews its entries.
packs.license_note: Repository-wide MIT license file, copyright 2026 Leonardo Flores.

packs.name: Build with Claude
packs.description: A Claude Code marketplace manifest that a host registers as an install source for the plugin packages the repository ships.
packs.installs: The repository's own Claude Code marketplace manifest at .claude-plugin/marketplace.json, declaring the marketplace schema and its owner, registered with /plugin marketplace add davepoon/buildwithclaude and then installed entry by entry with /plugin install <name>@buildwithclaude; each entry resolves to a directory under plugins/, and the README also documents copying agent and command Markdown files into ~/.claude/agents/ and ~/.claude/commands/ after a clone. This record pins the manifest and does not list, count, or review its entries.
packs.distribution_machinery: scripts/ holds Node tooling for the repository's own files: validate-all.js and the four per-type validators validate-subagents.js, validate-commands.js, validate-hooks.js, and validate-skills.js against four JSON schemas, generate-registry.js builds the site registry, and fetch-plugins.js with github-search-pagination.js collects external listings. web-ui/ is the project's own website. None of it is installed into a host.
packs.not_a_system: A marketplace manifest that lists other packs for installation; it is an install source, not a system, and this record never lists, counts, or reviews its entries.
packs.license_note: Repository-wide MIT license file, copyright 2025 davepoon.

packs.name: claude-code-tresor
packs.description: A development-workflow kit of skill, agent, subagent, and slash-command documents copied into a Claude Code configuration directory.
packs.installs: 8 SKILL.md skill directories under skills/ in three categories (development, documentation, security), 8 agent definitions under agents/ carried both as agents/<name>.md and as agents/<name>/agent.md, 133 further subagent definitions as agent.md files under subagents/, 24 slash-command Markdown files under commands/, and 6 prompt templates, 11 standards documents, and 10 worked examples under prompts/, standards/, and examples/. scripts/install.sh copies skills/, commands/, and agents/ into ~/.claude/skills/, ~/.claude/commands/, and ~/.claude/agents/, where Claude Code discovers them, and the remaining documents into ~/claude-code-resources/; the README documents the same copies by hand.
packs.distribution_machinery: scripts/install.sh backs up an existing ~/.claude/ directory, creates the discovery directories, and copies the pack's documents into them, with --skills-only, --commands-only, --agents-only, and --resources-only selectors; scripts/update.sh refreshes an existing install. commitlint.config.js is the repository's own commit tooling and is not installed.
packs.not_a_system: Owns no state it reads back and does no enforced work: everything installed is Markdown that Claude Code reads and executes with its own tools, and the only code it ships copies those files into the host's discovery directories.
packs.license_note: Repository-wide MIT license file, copyright 2025 Alireza Rezvani.

packs.name: obsidian-claude-pkm
packs.description: An Obsidian vault template with the skills, agents, rules, and host configuration a coding agent reads to maintain it.
packs.installs: A vault-template/ directory copied into a vault location: 13 SKILL.md skill directories, 4 agent definitions, 4 rule documents, and 1 output style under vault-template/.claude/, a plugin manifest at vault-template/.claude-plugin/plugin.json declaring commands, agents, skills, hooks, output styles, and rules, and a vault-template/.claude/settings.json carrying 19 permission allow rules and 3 deny rules, 7 environment variables, and three hook configurations (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, and a PostToolUse matcher on Write and Edit). The vault content is a root CLAUDE.md with a CLAUDE.local.md.template, 4 Goals documents, 3 note Templates, an example daily note, and an example project with its own CLAUDE.md. Claude Code reads the .claude/ tree from the vault root; Obsidian opens the same directory as a vault. github-actions/claude.yml is offered separately for a vault kept on GitHub.
packs.distribution_machinery: scripts/setup.sh and scripts/setup.bat copy vault-template/ into a chosen vault directory, and scripts/customize.sh rewrites the folder names the configuration refers to. The installed vault's own shipped shell files are .claude/hooks/session-init.sh, which exports path and date variables and prints vault status at session start; .claude/hooks/skill-discovery.sh, which prints the pack's own SKILL.md names and descriptions when a prompt mentions skills or help; .claude/hooks/auto-commit.sh, which runs git add and git commit over the vault after the host writes or edits a file, when GIT_AUTO_COMMIT is true; and .claude/scripts/statusline.sh.
packs.not_a_system: Owns no state it reads back through code it ships and does no enforced work: its skills, agents, and rules are Markdown that Claude Code executes with its own tools, two of its hooks only print the pack's own documents and vault status into the session, and the third commits the vault to git after the host has already written, which records what the host did rather than enforcing anything and which ADR 031 holds never qualifies a pack on its own.
packs.license_note: Repository-wide MIT license file, copyright 2024 Obsidian Claude PKM Contributors.

packs.name: Second Brain Starter
packs.description: One skill document and a set of Markdown memory templates a coding agent reads to draft a build plan for a personal assistant.
packs.installs: One skill directory, .claude/skills/create-second-brain-prd/, holding SKILL.md, a requirements template, a filled-in example of that template, and references/architecture-reference.md, plus 6 Markdown memory templates under templates/memory/ (BOOTSTRAP, HABITS, HEARTBEAT, MEMORY, SOUL, USER) and a placeholder for a daily directory. The README installs it by cloning the repository and copying that skill directory into a project's own .claude/skills/, where Claude Code discovers it. The tree contains no executable files.
packs.not_a_system: Owns no state it reads back and does no enforced work: the tree is fifteen files with no code in it, and the host agent is what reads the templates and writes the plan they describe.
packs.license_note: No LICENSE file is served at LICENSE, LICENSE.md, or LICENSE.txt and the README claims none; no reusable licence can be established and none is inferred.
